::: {.callout-note .part-overview icon=false}
## Why this part comes here

Persuasion, storytelling, and communication are related but not identical. The sequence moves from intentional model change, to narrative simulation, to the joint construction and repair of meaning.
:::

## Guiding questions

- What prevents an audience from updating?
- How should story and evidence be braided?
- How do people ground meaning, listen, disagree, and repair?

- **Chapter 25:** [Persuasion Is Model Updating](../chapters/25-persuasion-is-model-updating.qmd) — Changing minds requires more than adding facts — About 23 min
- **Chapter 26:** [Why Stories Move Minds](../chapters/26-why-stories-move-minds.qmd) — Narrative turns information into simulated meaning — About 20 min
- **Chapter 27:** [Building an Evidence-Aligned Story](../chapters/27-building-an-evidence-aligned-story.qmd) — ABT, STORY, evidence, applications, and ethics — About 27 min
- **Chapter 28:** [Communication Is Joint Inference](../chapters/28-communication-is-joint-inference.qmd) — Words are the visible tip; context and relationship do the hidden work — About 15 min
- **Chapter 29:** [The Art of Conversation and Repair](../chapters/29-the-art-of-conversation-and-repair.qmd) — Questions, layered listening, appreciation, support, disagreement, and apology — About 15 min

## Bridge to the next part

Negotiation is the capstone because it requires decision analysis, persuasion, communication, emotion regulation, and strategic interdependence at once.
